### [Agentforce Specialist V2] {Testing, Deployment & Maintenance} 1
Apex Logistics has built an AI-powered virtual assistant to help customers track shipments and resolve delivery exceptions. Before deploying it to their support portal, the quality assurance team needs a repeatable, data-driven method to verify the assistant's responses across hundreds of unique scenarios without manual effort. Which approach should they implement?
- [ ] A. Deploy the assistant to a small group of beta customers, collect feedback on incorrect answers for two weeks, and then manually correct the underlying instructions.
- [x] B. Upload a batch test manifest in JSON Lines format, then execute the validation pipeline to generate automated pass/fail metrics for every test case.
- [ ] C. Manually simulate conversations using the agent's playground interface and rely on senior QA analysts to approve each intent path individually.
> The correct approach is automated batch validation: uploading a structured test manifest containing input prompts and expected outputs lets the system run all test cases programmatically, compare actual responses to expected ones, and produce objective pass/fail metrics. This is scalable, repeatable, and removes human subjectivity, making it suitable for pre-deployment validation across many scenarios. Beta testing with post-deployment feedback (A) is reactive — it happens after customers are already exposed to the agent, relies on uncontrolled interactions, and doesn't scale to hundreds of scenarios. Manual simulation with analyst approval (C) is not scalable either: it's time-consuming, error-prone as test cases grow, and depends on subjective judgment rather than systematic automated comparison. [Fuente: examen de práctica del usuario, incluye explicación oficial del simulador]

### [Agentforce Specialist V2] {AI Agents} 2
A financial services firm has built an AI agent using a low-code orchestration tool. The agent has a "Process Investment Withdrawal" action. According to company policy, withdrawals are allowed only if the client's Risk Profile is "Aggressive." Currently, the agent relies on its base instructions to check this field, but it sometimes hallucinates authorization and tries to execute the withdrawal for "Conservative" clients, causing transaction errors. How can the specialist enforce a deterministic control that prevents the agent from even seeing the withdrawal action unless the client meets the eligibility rule?
- [x] A. Add a conditional availability rule directly on the "Process Investment Withdrawal" action so that the action is hidden from the agent unless Risk_Profile__c = "Aggressive".
- [ ] B. Rewrite the agent's system instructions to include a strict warning: "Never call withdrawal for Conservative clients" and hope the language model follows it.
- [ ] C. Configure a keyword filter that automatically blocks the words "withdrawal" or "redeem" from appearing in the user's message if the client is not Aggressive.
> The correct method is an action-level condition filter (availability rule) directly on the withdrawal action — a deterministic, programmatic guard the LLM cannot override, because the action is literally unavailable to the agent when the condition fails. This prevents hallucinated attempts and enforces the business rule at the orchestration layer with 100% reliability. System instructions (B) are non-deterministic: LLMs can ignore or misinterpret natural-language warnings, especially in long or ambiguous context, so the same hallucination risk persists. A keyword filter (C) is trivial to bypass by rephrasing ("cash out my investments," "take my money out") and doesn't enforce the underlying field-based eligibility rule — it only reacts to surface wording. Gemela conceptual dentro de este banco: caso "Issue Refund" / Account_Tier = "Platinum" (Action Condition filter). [Fuente: examen de práctica del usuario, incluye explicación oficial del simulador]

### [Agentforce Specialist V2] {AI Agents} 3
A healthcare provider is building a custom agent that calls an Apex action to update patient medication lists. The action requires an input parameter that accepts multiple medication names (a list of text values). The specialist is defining the action's metadata in the agent's asset library. Which complex data type name should they use to correctly map a list of strings to the Apex parameter?
- [x] A. lightning__textType
- [ ] B. apex__TextList
- [ ] C. lightning__stringType
> lightning__textType is the valid standard Lightning type for text values in Agentforce action metadata (confirmed in Salesforce's official Lightning Types reference: the canonical list of standard types is booleanType, dateType, dateTimeType, dateTimeStringType, integerType, multilineTextType, numberType, objectType, richTextType, textType, timeType, urlType — there is no separate "stringType"). When an Apex parameter is a collection (List<String>), Agentforce still maps it using the same base type name with collection cardinality applied, rather than a distinct "list" type name — so lightning__textType is correct for a list of medication names too. apex__TextList doesn't follow Salesforce's lightning__ naming convention and isn't a recognized type; lightning__stringType doesn't appear in the official standard types list at all (developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/lightning-types/guide/lightning-types.html). [Verificado con búsqueda web — confianza alta en que textType es válido y stringType no existe; confianza media en el detalle exacto de cómo se marca la cardinalidad de lista, ya que la doc no lo especifica de forma explícita en el contexto de Apex actions.]

### [Agentforce Specialist V2] {Data 360 Fundamentals} 4
A logistics company wants to upload several warehouse safety manuals (PDFs) to a new Agentforce Data Library. They plan to use advanced processing with Intelligent Context to optimize chunking and parsing based on document layout. How should they proceed to let the system first determine the optimal indexing configuration before processing the full document set?
- [x] A. Upload up to five PDFs, each no larger than 10 MB, so the system can analyze structure and recommend chunk size, overlap, and parsing strategy.
- [ ] B. Manually enable "Intelligent Context" in the library settings before uploading any files.
- [ ] C. Upload all PDFs (any size) at once; the system will automatically detect and apply optimal indexing as a background job.
> The recommended practice for Intelligent Context advanced processing is to upload a small representative sample first so the system can evaluate document structure (tables, layout, nesting) and propose optimal indexing parameters — chunk size, overlap, parsing strategy — before scaling up to the full document set, rather than committing an entire large batch to a single configuration upfront. There is no manual toggle to "enable" Intelligent Context in library settings — it's automatically considered during upload/processing when conditions (like file type and advanced parsing) are met, so option B isn't actionable. Uploading everything at once (C) skips the evaluation step and risks a suboptimal configuration being applied at scale, plus potential processing delays with larger files. [Verificado con búsqueda web: confirmé que Intelligent Context es una función real de Data 360/Agentforce (parsing basado en LLM que preserva estructura de tablas/layout antes del "flattening" tradicional de PDFs), pero NO pude confirmar el límite numérico exacto ("hasta 5 PDFs, ≤10 MB cada uno") en documentación oficial indexada — la página de Salesforce Help es JS-rendered y no se pudo inspeccionar el texto completo. Confianza media en ese detalle específico; verificar el límite exacto en el org o en la doc oficial antes de memorizarlo para el examen.]

### [Agentforce Specialist V2] {Data 360 Fundamentals} 5
A global retailer runs a customer help center powered by an Agentforce Service Agent. The legal team maintains a Salesforce Knowledge base of return policies, warranty terms, and regulatory disclosures. These articles are updated frequently by subject matter experts. The agent must always retrieve only the most current, published content and answer customer questions using semantic understanding. What is the simplest, most maintainable solution?
- [ ] A. Build a custom Apex REST endpoint that queries the Knowledge object and returns matching articles via keyword search; call this endpoint from a sub-action every time the agent responds.
- [x] B. Connect an Agentforce Data Library directly to the Salesforce Knowledge base, filter for PublishStatus = 'Published', and let the agent use retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) with semantic search.
- [ ] C. Configure a custom retriever in Einstein AI Studio that indexes Knowledge articles into a separate vector database and schedule a nightly sync to catch updates.
> A Data Library connected directly to Salesforce Knowledge with a PublishStatus filter is the simplest, lowest-maintenance solution: it reflects Knowledge updates in near real time, uses semantic RAG retrieval, and needs no custom code or external indexing. PublishStatus is a real field on Knowledge article versions with values Draft, Online (Published), and Archived, so filtering on it to only surface published content is a standard, supported pattern. A custom Apex REST endpoint with keyword search (A) only matches exact terms — no semantic understanding — and adds ongoing development/maintenance burden. A custom retriever syncing to an external vector database on a nightly schedule (C) adds unnecessary complexity, cost, and sync latency, which directly conflicts with the requirement to always serve the most current published content — the native Data Library-to-Knowledge integration already handles this out of the box. [Verificado con búsqueda web: confirmé que PublishStatus es un campo real en KnowledgeArticleVersion con esos tres valores (Draft/Online/Archived); el resto de la lógica es consistente con el patrón de Data Library + Knowledge ya establecido en este banco.]

### [Agentforce Specialist V2] {Prompt Engineering} 6
An airline's customer service team needs a Flex prompt template to generate post-call summaries for baggage issue cases. The summary must follow a strict four-part format: "Problem," "Actions Taken," "Resolution," and "Next Steps." If no next step exists, the summary must state "No further action needed." Which approach ensures the language model consistently produces this exact structure?
- [ ] A. Use a prompt-triggered flow to parse the raw LLM output and then reformat it using Apex string manipulation.
- [x] B. Include explicit section headings and conditional phrasing instructions in the prompt's "Format" and "Constraints" sections.
- [ ] C. Apply chain-of-thought reasoning with a step that first outlines the four headings, then fills content beneath each.
> The most direct and reliable way to enforce a specific output structure is to define it clearly in the prompt itself, using explicit headings ("Problem:", "Actions Taken:", etc.) in the Format section and conditional phrasing rules (e.g., "if no next step exists, state 'No further action needed'") in the Constraints section. This guides the LLM to produce the exact structure directly, without extra code or multi-step techniques — consistent with the RTCCF (Role/Task/Context/Constraints/Format) prompt design pattern already established for Salesforce prompt templates. Post-processing with a flow and Apex string manipulation (A) adds latency, complexity, and maintenance overhead for something the prompt itself can already guarantee. Chain-of-thought reasoning (C) is meant for multi-step reasoning problems, not for enforcing a simple output template, and would likely leak extraneous reasoning text ("First, I will outline the headings...") into the final summary, violating the clean-structure requirement. [Consistente con el patrón RTCCF y las mejores prácticas de Prompt Builder ya documentadas en este banco; no requirió verificación adicional.]

### [Agentforce Specialist V2] {Multi-Agent Orchestration} 7
A large manufacturing company has deployed three specialized Employee Agents: Facilities Request, IT Helpdesk, and Benefits Inquiry. Employees often pick the wrong agent (e.g., asking the Benefits agent to unlock a laptop), leading to failed interactions and frustration. Leadership wants a single, unified entry point that automatically understands intent and routes to the correct specialized agent, without requiring employees to choose from a list. Which architecture should be implemented?
- [x] A. A single orchestrator agent that uses a Multi-Agent (SOMA) design to interpret user input and delegate to the appropriate specialized agent dynamically.
- [ ] B. A validation rule on the Agent Session object that blocks mismatched requests and prompts the user to reselect the correct agent.
- [ ] C. A standalone Multi-Agent system where each agent includes a first message asking the user to confirm their department before proceeding.
> A Single Org Multi-Agent (SOMA) architecture uses a Supervisor/orchestrator agent as a single front door: the Atlas Reasoning Engine reviews each specialist agent's description, instructions, and available actions to determine which one is best equipped for the request, then routes and delegates dynamically — no manual selection needed, and all specialists share native access to the same org data (Cases, Contacts, Data Cloud context) without extra auth flows. A validation rule on Agent Session (B) only rejects mismatched requests after the fact — the employee still has to guess which agent to use first and just gets an error instead of a resolution. A standalone multi-agent setup where each agent asks the user to confirm their department (C) doesn't remove the guesswork either — it just moves the manual selection into the conversation and adds friction to every interaction. [Verificado con búsqueda web: SOMA (Single Org Multi-Agent) es un patrón de arquitectura real de Agentforce, con un agente Supervisor/orquestador que enruta a agentes especialistas dentro del mismo org — confirmado en salesforcediary.com y architect.salesforce.com/docs/architect/fundamentals/guide/enterprise-agentic-architecture.]

### [Agentforce Specialist V2] {Data 360 Fundamentals} 8
A retail chain wants to ground an Agentforce agent with real-time inventory data stored in an external warehouse management system. They cannot duplicate the data into Data 360 due to storage costs and the need for millisecond-accurate stock levels. Which Data 360 capability allows virtual, real-time access to external structured data without ingestion?
- [x] A. Zero Copy data federation
- [ ] B. Scheduled data streams with incremental refresh
- [ ] C. Semantic index on external content
> Zero Copy is Data 360's data federation technology: it queries external systems (data warehouses/lakes like Snowflake, Databricks, Redshift, BigQuery) live, using metadata management and query pushdown, without ever creating, persisting, or hosting a copy of the tables inside Data 360. This gives near real-time access and avoids storage costs and duplication — exactly matching the requirement for millisecond-accurate stock levels without ingestion. Scheduled data streams with incremental refresh (B) still import and duplicate data into Data 360, and can't guarantee accuracy between sync intervals. A semantic index on external content (C) requires the data to already be indexed into Data 360 first, meaning ingestion/duplication has already happened — it doesn't provide the "no ingestion" virtual access the requirement calls for. [Verificado con búsqueda web: "Zero Copy data federation" es el término oficial exacto usado por Salesforce (salesforce.com/data/connectivity/zero-copy, Trailhead "Get Started with Zero Copy Data Federation"), con dos modos: query federation y file federation.]

### [Agentforce Specialist V2] {Data 360 Fundamentals} 9
In the context of retrieval-augmented generation, what is the primary purpose of converting a text chunk into a vector embedding?
- [ ] A. To reduce the storage footprint of the original document by compressing it into a smaller numeric form.
- [x] B. To represent the chunk's semantic meaning as a set of numbers, enabling similarity searches based on conceptual closeness rather than exact keywords.
- [ ] C. To encrypt the chunk so that it can be stored securely in a vector database without exposing plain text.
> Vectorization transforms text into a dense numerical representation (an embedding) that captures semantic meaning in a high-dimensional space. This lets the retrieval system find content that is conceptually similar to a query even when the exact wording differs — the foundation of semantic (meaning-based) search that RAG relies on, as opposed to plain keyword matching. Embeddings are not a compression technique (A): they're typically a fixed-size numeric vector that adds storage overhead rather than shrinking the original text. Vectorization is also not encryption (C) — it's a representation built for semantic comparison, not for security, and doesn't prevent anyone from reconstructing or comparing meaning from the vector. [Concepto fundamental de RAG/embeddings, consistente con el resto del banco; no requirió verificación adicional.]

### [Agentforce Specialist V2] {Prompt Engineering} 10
A support manager needs to build a prompt in Prompt Builder that generates a post-call resolution note. The note must: Summarize the customer's issue, troubleshooting steps, and final resolution. Be at most three sentences. Use non-technical language. If no resolution was reached, explicitly state "Escalated to tier 2." Which combination of prompt constructs directly addresses all these requirements?
- [ ] A. Role, Task, Format, and Output Validator
- [x] B. Task, Context, Constraints, and Format
- [ ] C. Context, LLM Temperature, Token Limit, and Format
> The requirements map directly onto the RTCCF prompt design elements: Task (what to generate — the resolution note), Context (the case data grounding the summary — issue, troubleshooting, resolution), Constraints (the three-sentence limit, non-technical language, and the conditional "Escalated to tier 2" rule), and Format (the desired output structure). Together these give the LLM complete, unambiguous guidance to produce consistent, rule-compliant output. "Output Validator" (A) isn't a prompt-authoring construct that guides generation — it's a post-generation check — and Role is optional here since this is deterministic formatting, not persona-driven writing; this combo also drops Context and Constraints entirely. LLM Temperature and Token Limit (C) are model/runtime parameters, not content instructions — Temperature controls randomness and Token Limit only caps length, neither can express conditional logic like "state Escalated to tier 2 if unresolved," and Context alone can't substitute for Task and Format. [Consistente con el patrón RTCCF de Prompt Builder ya documentado en este banco; no requirió verificación adicional.]

### [Agentforce Specialist V2] {Governance & Observability} 11
A national utility company's customer agent has been running for six weeks. The observability dashboard shows the "Billing Dispute" intent cluster has low quality, with the reason "ambiguous subagent match." Session traces confirm the planner routes billing disputes to the "Payment Arrangement" subagent on most turns. What is the most effective solution?
- [ ] A. Reduce the number of subagents from 10 to 4 by merging billing and payment intents into a single subagent.
- [x] B. Rewrite the classification descriptions of the two overlapping subagents to eliminate semantic confusion and create clear boundaries.
- [ ] C. Add a system instruction that says "Never send billing disputes to payment arrangement subagent" and place it in every subagent's prompt.
> The planner (Atlas Reasoning Engine) selects a subagent primarily by comparing the user's input against each subagent's Topic Name and Classification Description — this is the same mechanism already established elsewhere in this bank. Misrouting between "Billing Dispute" and "Payment Arrangement" here is a symptom of semantic overlap between those two subagents' classification descriptions, so the direct fix is to rewrite them to be mutually exclusive and unambiguous, resolving the root cause without losing specialization. Merging the subagents (A) is a blunt workaround: it eliminates the symptom by removing the distinction entirely, but the merged subagent can still mishandle nuanced intents and functionality is reduced. A system instruction telling the LLM to "never" route one way (C) is non-deterministic — the LLM can still ignore or misapply it, especially while the underlying descriptions still conflict, so the same ambiguous-match problem persists. [Consistente con el mecanismo de selección de topic/subagent (Topic Name + Classification Description) ya documentado en la pregunta #1 de este banco; no requirió verificación adicional.]

### [Agentforce Specialist V2] {Data 360 Fundamentals} 12
A medical lab must ensure its support agent always provides the most current version of testing procedure documents. Outdated content could lead to incorrect diagnoses. What should the specialist recommend?
- [x] A. Connect a knowledge-based data library to Salesforce Knowledge, which automatically retrieves only the published version of each article using native version control.
- [ ] B. Store all procedure files in a file-based data library and manually delete old versions each time a new one is uploaded.
- [ ] C. Add a "valid until" date field to each document and instruct the agent in its system prompt to ignore documents past that date.
> Salesforce Knowledge has built-in versioning and publishing workflows (Draft/Published-Online/Archived, as already confirmed elsewhere in this bank via the PublishStatus field). A knowledge-based data library connects directly to Knowledge and respects article status, so it deterministically retrieves only the currently published version of each procedure document — no manual upkeep, no reliance on the LLM interpreting anything. A file-based library with manual deletion (B) is error-prone and doesn't scale: file-based libraries have no native version tracking, so a missed manual cleanup leaves outdated, potentially unsafe procedures retrievable. A "valid until" field enforced only through system-prompt instructions (C) is non-deterministic — the LLM can still retrieve or reference an expired document despite the instruction, which is an unacceptable compliance risk in a medical/diagnostic context. [Consistente con el mecanismo de Data Library + Salesforce Knowledge + PublishStatus ya verificado en este banco; no requirió verificación adicional.]

### [Agentforce Specialist V2] {Multi-Agent Orchestration} 13
A support team is building an Omni-Flow to route incoming chat messages from a retail website to live agents after the automated agent cannot resolve the issue. Which Omni-Flow element should they use to assign the conversation to an available agent based on skills and capacity?
- [x] A. Route Work
- [ ] B. Allocate to Agent
- [ ] C. Send to Queue
> Route Work is the real Omni-Flow action used to route a work item to an agent: it lets you specify the service channel, routing configuration, and skill requirement list, then filters reps by skills and available capacity before offering the work to the first eligible rep — this is the standard skills-based routing mechanism in Omni-Channel Flow. "Allocate to Agent" (B) isn't part of the Omni-Flow element palette; it doesn't exist. "Send to Queue" (C) only places the work item in a queue — it doesn't complete the assignment to a specific available agent by itself. [Verificado con búsqueda web: "Route Work" es un elemento real de Omni-Channel Flow (help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=service.omnichannel_flows.htm), que aplica skill requirements y filtra por capacidad antes de ofrecer el work item al primer rep elegible.]

### [Agentforce Specialist V2] {Data 360 Fundamentals} 14
An auto parts retailer has a knowledge base with articles categorized by vehicle type (Car, Truck, Motorcycle). They want the agent to retrieve only Car articles. What does enabling "Filter by Knowledge Data Categories" do in a knowledge-based data library?
- [ ] A. It adds the selected category names as metadata tags to each article to improve search ranking.
- [x] B. It limits the indexing process to include only articles assigned to the selected categories, excluding all others from retrieval.
- [ ] C. It creates separate vector indexes for each category and searches them in parallel.
> When configuring the Knowledge settings for a data library, an admin can filter which articles get grounded by data category (as well as by channel or article type), alongside the standard "published only" filter. This category filter is applied at ingestion/indexing time: only articles assigned to the selected data categories (e.g., Car) get indexed into the library's search index, so articles outside those categories (Truck, Motorcycle) are never indexed and therefore can never be retrieved — improving precision instead of relying on the LLM to sort articles by category at query time. It does not add metadata tags to articles (A) — it filters based on the category assignments the articles already have. It also doesn't create separate parallel indexes per category (C) — there's a single index, and the category filter simply narrows what goes into it. [Verificado con búsqueda web: el filtrado por Data Category en la configuración de Knowledge de un Data Library es una función real y documentada (help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ai.data_library_select_fields.htm), aplicada al indexar/groundear artículos.]

### [Agentforce Specialist V2] {Multi-Agent Orchestration} 15
A travel agency wants to route incoming Facebook Messenger messages to an automated agent that can handle flight changes, hotel bookings, and cancellation requests. Which destination is a valid Omni-Channel routing option for a messaging channel?
- [ ] A. External chatbot via custom API
- [x] B. Agentforce Service Agent
- [ ] C. Legacy Einstein Bot
> Agentforce Service Agent is a native, selectable routing destination for Omni-Channel messaging channels — including Facebook Messenger and other Enhanced Messaging channels — so incoming conversations can be routed directly to it via Route Work (or equivalent routing configuration), where the agent's conversational AI handles the request end to end. An external chatbot reached through a custom API (A) isn't a native Omni-Flow routing destination; it would require custom integration work rather than being a standard, out-of-the-box option. Legacy Einstein Bots (C) use a different invocation mechanism (bot deployment on a channel) rather than being selected as an Omni-Channel routing destination in this pattern. [Consistente con el patrón de enrutamiento de Omni-Channel hacia Agentforce Service Agent en canales de mensajería ya documentado en este banco; no requirió verificación adicional más allá de lo ya confirmado sobre Route Work.]

### [Agentforce Specialist V2] {Testing, Deployment & Maintenance} 16
A music streaming service deployed a Service Agent handling playlist recovery, account cancellation, and audio quality settings. After updating the Account Cancellation subagent instructions to include a retention offer flow, some cancellation questions started routing to the Playlist Recovery subagent. The team needs to diagnose the regression before full deployment. Which approach is most systematic and objective?
- [x] A. Run the stored test suite in Testing Center against the modified agent, review Subagent Pass % metrics to identify regressions, then add test cases for the retention flow.
- [ ] B. Ask three support agents to manually test 20 conversation paths each and report misrouting.
- [ ] C. Deploy to 5% of production users and monitor the misrouting rate in the observability dashboard for two days.
> Testing Center runs the stored regression suite automatically and reports objective pass-rate metrics per dimension — the results dashboard shows Topic/Subagent Pass %, Action Pass %, and Response Pass % (the "Topic" label is being renamed to "Subagent" following Agentforce's April 2026 terminology update, already noted elsewhere in this bank) — so a regression like cancellation questions misrouting to Playlist Recovery shows up immediately as a drop in that specific pass rate, without guesswork. Extending the suite with new test cases for the retention flow then locks in coverage so future changes are validated automatically, with no production risk. Manual testing by support agents (B) is subjective, doesn't scale, and isn't repeatable as a regression check. Deploying to a slice of production and watching the observability dashboard (C) is reactive — it exposes real customers to the regression for days before it's caught, instead of catching it pre-deployment. [Verificado con búsqueda web: el dashboard de resultados de Testing Center sí reporta pass % por dimensión (Trailhead "Understanding Agentforce Testing Center Results" confirma "Topic Pass %, Action Pass %, Response Pass %"); el nombre exacto "Subagent Pass %" es una inferencia razonable dado el rebranding topic→subagent ya documentado en este banco, pero no lo vi verbatim así en la fuente.]

### [Agentforce Specialist V2] {Multi-Agent Orchestration} 17
An online pet supply store is building an agent to capture a customer's preferred delivery date during a conversation. The specialist declares a variable in Agent Script as delivery_date: string = "" (without the mutable keyword). Later, the agent tries to update it using @utils.setVariables. What happens at runtime?
- [ ] A. The variable is automatically mutable because it is a string; the update succeeds.
- [x] B. The variable remains read-only; the update attempt has no effect because mutable was omitted.
- [ ] C. The declaration causes a syntax error and the agent fails to publish.
> In Agent Script, variables are read-only by default — the `mutable` keyword is optional and must be explicitly included to let the agent change a variable's value (e.g., `mutable string = ""`). Without it, the declaration is valid syntax, but the variable can never be written to, so an @utils.setVariables call targeting it has no effect at runtime. Data type has nothing to do with mutability (A) — a string is just as read-only by default as any other type; only the `mutable` keyword changes that. And since the syntax itself is valid, there's no publish-time syntax error (C) — the agent just won't be able to capture the delivery date as intended, which is a logic bug, not a compile error. [Verificado con búsqueda web: confirmado en la Agent Script Developer Guide oficial (developer.salesforce.com/docs/ai/agentforce/guide/ascript-ref-variables.html) — "mutable" es opcional y habilita escritura; sin él, el valor nunca cambia.]

### [Agentforce Specialist V2] {Governance & Observability} 18
A credit union's agent frequently routes "loan application status" requests to the "credit card application" subagent. This misrouting has increased average handling time. The manager needs a quick solution that preserves the agent's ability to handle complex, branching conversations. What should the specialist do?
- [x] A. Add a deterministic routing hint to the loan status subagent's classification description, such as "only for loan status, not credit cards," to guide the planner without rigid rules.
- [ ] B. Merge the two subagents into one to eliminate the routing decision entirely.
- [ ] C. Insert a system instruction that says "Never send loan status questions to credit card subagent" at the top of the agent's configuration.
> This is the same misrouting pattern already established in this bank: the planner selects a subagent by comparing the user's input against each subagent's Topic Name and Classification Description, so overlapping or ambiguous language between "loan application status" and "credit card application" descriptions is the root cause. Rewriting the classification description with a clear, distinguishing hint fixes the ambiguity directly while keeping each subagent specialized and the planner free to handle nuanced, branching conversations. Merging the subagents (B) removes the routing decision but sacrifices specialization, likely degrading handling of both request types. A blanket system instruction (C) is non-deterministic — the LLM can still ignore or misweigh it, especially while the two classification descriptions still overlap, so the misrouting risk remains. [Consistente con el mecanismo de selección de subagent (Topic Name + Classification Description) ya verificado en la pregunta #1 y en la #11 de este banco; no requirió verificación adicional.]

### [Agentforce Specialist V2] {Data 360 Fundamentals} 19
A logistics firm is ingesting large shipping contract PDFs into an agent's data library. They need to understand document processing to optimize retrieval. What is a key characteristic of the chunking process?
- [x] A. Chunking splits large documents into smaller, indexable passages, each vectorized for semantic matching to user queries.
- [ ] B. Chunking compresses each document into a single vector that represents the entire file's average meaning.
- [ ] C. Chunking sends the first 500 characters of each document to the LLM and discards the rest to save tokens.
> Chunking divides a large document into smaller passages, each of which is independently vectorized and indexed, so retrieval can match a user query against the specific passage that's semantically relevant rather than the document as a whole. This granularity is what makes precise, meaning-based retrieval possible for long documents like shipping contracts. A single averaged vector per document (B) would collapse all that granularity, making it impossible to pinpoint a specific clause or section. Chunking also doesn't discard content to save tokens (C) — the whole point is to preserve all of the document's content, just split across multiple indexed, retrievable passages instead of truncating it. [Concepto fundamental de RAG/chunking ya cubierto en varias preguntas de este banco (ej. #57 sobre chunk size y cláusulas legales anidadas); no requirió verificación adicional.]

### [Agentforce Specialist V2] {Prompt Engineering} 20
A real estate investment firm is creating a prompt template for an agent that needs to reference property inspection records related to an account. The specialist wants to include fields from the Inspections__r related list on the Account object. What is the correct procedure in Prompt Builder?
- [x] A. Select the Inspections related list from the Account object, then use the field picker to choose specific merge fields from that list to include in the prompt.
- [ ] B. Write an Apex method that queries the inspection records and returns JSON, then reference that method in the prompt.
- [ ] C. Hard-code the inspection field names as literal text in the prompt and rely on the LLM to infer the relationship.
> Prompt Builder natively supports grounding on related list data: after selecting the object (Account), the specialist can add the Inspections related list and use the field picker to choose specific merge fields from those child records to include in the prompt — a fully declarative process, no code required. This is the same related-list merge field mechanism already covered in this bank (e.g., the Activities-related-list-is-polymorphic caveat) — related lists work this way in general, just with object-specific exceptions like polymorphic fields. Writing a custom Apex method to query and return JSON (B) is unnecessary complexity Prompt Builder already handles out of the box. Hard-coding field names as literal text (C) provides no dynamic data binding at all — the LLM would just see static text, not actual record values, so it couldn't ground a real answer in the customer's actual inspection data. [Consistente con el mecanismo de related list merge fields en Prompt Builder ya documentado en este banco; no requirió verificación adicional.]

### [Agentforce Specialist V2] {AI Agents} 21
A logistics company is building an agent to handle delivery address changes. The agent must first validate the customer's order number against an external ERP system, and only after successful validation should it call an existing Apex action that updates the address. The validation step is already configured as a separate action. Which implementation approach should the specialist recommend?
- [ ] A. Add a new instruction to the agent's global system prompt saying "after validation, call the address update action" and rely on the LLM to sequence correctly.
- [ ] B. Create a separate subagent for address updates, pass the validation result as a session variable, and let the second subagent's instructions check the variable before proceeding.
- [x] C. Within the same action flow that performs validation, add a deterministic conditional step that only invokes the address update Apex action if the validation response contains a success flag.
> Keeping the validation-then-update logic inside a single deterministic flow — with a conditional branch that only calls the address update Apex action when the validation response carries a success flag — guarantees the correct order every time, since it never depends on the LLM to decide when or whether to call the update action. This mirrors the hybrid reasoning principle already established in this bank: business-critical sequencing (validate before mutating data) belongs in deterministic logic, not in natural-language instructions. A global system-prompt instruction telling the LLM to sequence the calls (A) is non-deterministic — the LLM could still call the update action without validation succeeding, which is exactly the failure mode this design needs to prevent. Splitting the work across a second subagent that reads a session variable (B) adds unnecessary architectural complexity and introduces a cross-action state dependency (the variable has to reliably persist and be checked) instead of just keeping the guarded logic together in one flow. [Consistente con el principio de hybrid reasoning / lógica determinista para pasos de negocio críticos ya verificado en este banco (casos "Issue Refund"/Account_Tier y KYC); no requirió verificación adicional.]

### [Agentforce Specialist V2] {Multi-Agent Orchestration} 22
A hospital network uses Agentforce for patient appointment scheduling. It also runs a separate AI system from a different vendor for managing operating room inventory. The hospital wants the Agentforce scheduler to autonomously request supply checks from the inventory system when scheduling surgeries. Which open standard protocol is specifically designed for this cross-vendor agent collaboration?
- [ ] A. Inter-Agent Messaging Protocol (IMP)
- [x] B. Agent-to-Agent (A2A) protocol
- [ ] C. Cross-Platform Agent Bridge (CPAB)
> Ya confirmado varias veces en este banco: el Agent-to-Agent (A2A) protocol es el estándar abierto diseñado específicamente para que agentes autónomos e independientes de distintos vendors se descubran, negocien y deleguen tareas entre sí de forma segura — exactamente el escenario de un scheduler de Agentforce pidiendo autónomamente un chequeo de inventario a un sistema de IA de otro proveedor. "Inter-Agent Messaging Protocol (IMP)" y "Cross-Platform Agent Bridge (CPAB)" no son estándares reales; son nombres inventados para esta pregunta (patrón de distractor ya visto: nombres que suenan plausibles pero no existen, como "Prompt Execute User" o "apex__TextList" en otras preguntas de este banco). [Ya verificado en preguntas previas de este banco (A2A) — no requirió nueva verificación.]

### [Agentforce Specialist V2] {Data 360 Fundamentals} 23
Before deploying a RAG-based agent to answer employee HR policy questions, a specialist wants to test whether a custom retriever returns the most relevant sections of HR documents for sample queries, without writing any code. Which tool should they use?
- [x] A. Retriever Playground
- [ ] B. HR Document Tester
- [ ] C. Retrieval Quality Console
> The Retriever Playground is a no-code testing environment for custom retrievers — a specialist enters sample queries and inspects exactly which chunks come back, with relevance scores, before ever wiring the retriever into an agent or prompt template. Best practice is to validate a retriever here (or via a prompt template preview) before assigning it to an agent. "HR Document Tester" and "Retrieval Quality Console" are not real Agentforce/Data 360 tools — invented distractor names, the same pattern seen elsewhere in this bank (e.g., "Prompt Execute User"). [Verificado con búsqueda web: aunque no aparece en la documentación oficial más indexada, sí hay menciones reales de "Retriever Playground" en foros de la comunidad de Salesforce (Trailblazer Community) describiendo su uso para probar retrievers con scores de relevancia antes de usarlos en un agente — confianza media-alta.]

### [Agentforce Specialist V2] {Data 360 Fundamentals} 24
In a knowledge-based data library connected to a Salesforce Knowledge base, what is the primary functional difference between the fields labeled "searchable metadata" and "content body"?
- [x] A. Searchable metadata fields help the retriever locate the correct article via concise keywords, while the content body provides the detailed text that grounds the AI's response.
- [ ] B. Searchable metadata fields store the full article text for retrieval, while the content body contains a short summary for preview.
- [ ] C. Searchable metadata fields are used only for article categorization, while the content body is used only for relevance scoring.
> This maps onto the Identifying Fields vs. Content Fields distinction already established elsewhere in this bank: concise, indexable fields (title, keywords, article number) are used to locate the correct article, while the full body/content field supplies the detailed text that grounds and enriches the AI's actual response. Option B reverses the roles (a short field can't hold "full article text," and the content body isn't just a "preview summary"). Option C is too narrow — both field types can factor into relevance/retrieval, and categorization isn't the sole purpose of metadata fields. [Concepto consistente con "Identifying Fields vs Content Fields" ya verificado en este banco; los nombres exactos "searchable metadata" / "content body" usados en el enunciado son descriptivos y no necesariamente los nombres literales de la UI, pero el comportamiento descrito es correcto.]

### [Agentforce Specialist V2] {Prompt Engineering} 25
A specialist creates a new Field Generation prompt template for the Lead object, targeting a custom field Lead_Score_AI__c. After saving, testing, and activating the template, they open a Lead record and see that Lead_Score_AI__c behaves like a normal editable field without the Sparkle icon. What critical step did they miss?
- [ ] A. They forgot to assign the "Field Generation User" permission set to their user.
- [x] B. They forgot to edit the Lead record page in Lightning App Builder and associate the custom field with the prompt template.
- [ ] C. They forgot to run the "Refresh Field Generation Cache" scheduled job.
> Same root cause already documented in this bank for the Case/AI_Analysis__c scenario: activating a Field Generation prompt template isn't enough by itself — the target field must also be explicitly associated with the prompt template on the Lightning record page (via Lightning App Builder). Skipping that step leaves the field behaving as a normal editable field with no Sparkle icon, regardless of object (Lead here, Case in the earlier version of this question). "Field Generation User" isn't a real permission set (A) — Field Generation relies on standard object/field permissions — and there's no "Refresh Field Generation Cache" scheduled job (C); this is a one-time declarative configuration step, not a batch process. [Mismo mecanismo ya verificado en este banco para el caso Case/AI_Analysis__c; consistente, no requirió nueva verificación.]

### [Agentforce Specialist V2] {Governance & Observability} 26
A specialist is troubleshooting an agent that makes up fake product SKUs in its responses. The agent uses an action with a prompt template that includes a knowledge retriever. What is the most appropriate first step to diagnose the root cause?
- [x] A. Check the retrieved chunks in the resolved prompt output to see if the LLM is generating SKUs not present in the grounding data.
- [ ] B. Add a system instruction that says "NEVER invent SKUs" in bold and re-test.
- [ ] C. Verify that the subagent's classification description has a high confidence threshold.
> Hallucinations like fabricated SKUs typically trace back to a grounding gap — either the retriever isn't returning the chunks that actually contain the correct SKUs, or the LLM is generating content beyond what the retrieved chunks support. Inspecting the resolved prompt (what was actually sent to the LLM, including the retrieved chunks) is the direct, evidence-based way to confirm whether the fabricated SKUs exist anywhere in the grounding data — this mirrors the "grounding data is incorrect or incomplete" root-cause pattern already established elsewhere in this bank for underperforming generative outputs. A bolded "NEVER invent SKUs" instruction (B) doesn't fix a grounding gap and doesn't make the LLM deterministic — it's just another non-deterministic instruction the model can still ignore. Classification description confidence thresholds (C) affect subagent/topic routing, not what content gets generated once inside a response — unrelated to this failure mode. [Consistente con el patrón de troubleshooting de grounding/alucinaciones ya establecido en este banco; no requirió verificación adicional.]

### [Agentforce Specialist V2] {Testing, Deployment & Maintenance} 27
A specialist tests an agent connected to a data library. The agent retrieves the correct information but presents it as raw XML markup instead of natural, grammatically correct sentences. Which quality evaluation metric would score poorly in this scenario?
- [x] A. Coherence
- [ ] B. Completeness
- [ ] C. Conciseness
> Coherence is a real Agentforce evaluation metric (already confirmed elsewhere in this bank alongside Instruction Adherence) that measures whether a response is grammatically correct, logically structured, and reads naturally/conversationally — raw XML markup fails exactly that bar, since it has no natural-language grammar or flow, even though the underlying information is accurate. Completeness (B) measures whether all the required information is present, not how it's formatted — the data is all there, just poorly presented, so completeness wouldn't be the metric that suffers. Conciseness (C) measures brevity; raw XML could even be "concise" while still being completely incoherent, so it doesn't capture this failure either. [Coherence e Instruction Adherence ya confirmadas como métricas reales de evaluación en este banco (caso "De-escalation Framework" custom evaluation); no requirió verificación adicional.]

### [Agentforce Specialist V2] {Data 360 Fundamentals} 28
A university needs a service agent to ground its answers using both student handbook PDFs (file-based) and a knowledge base of course catalog articles. Which type of retriever should the specialist configure?
- [ ] A. Multi-source retriever
- [x] B. Ensemble retriever
- [ ] C. Hybrid retriever
> Already established in this bank: Einstein Studio offers Individual Retrievers (one index, with its own filters) and Ensemble Retrievers, which combine and re-rank results from multiple underlying retrievers — exactly what's needed to ground answers on both file-based PDFs and a separate knowledge-based index in a single query, simplifying the prompt template so it doesn't need to reference each retriever individually. "Multi-source retriever" (A) isn't a real Agentforce retriever type — Ensemble is the correct term. "Hybrid retriever" (C) refers to a different concept in this space — combining keyword and semantic search within a single retrieval — not to combining multiple distinct data sources. [Ya verificado en este banco (Ensemble Retriever, caso de tres search indexes de Universal Containers); consistente, no requirió nueva verificación.]

### [Agentforce Specialist V2] {Testing, Deployment & Maintenance} 29
A specialty coffee retailer builds an agent in a developer sandbox to handle loyalty point inquiries. The agent uses a custom Apex action that calls an external rewards API. After deploying all components (agent, Apex class, permission sets) to production using a metadata deployment, the agent fails to respond to any test messages. The Apex action is active and the API endpoint is reachable. What is the most likely missing step?
- [ ] A. The agent's "Production Ready" checkbox must be selected in the sandbox before deployment, otherwise the agent deploys in a suspended state.
- [x] B. The specialist must manually activate the agent in the production environment because deployment does not preserve the active/inactive status.
- [ ] C. The external API requires a different authentication certificate in production; the specialist must re-upload the certificate and update the named credential.
> An agent's active/inactive status is not preserved by deployment (change set or metadata API) — Salesforce's own deployment guidance explicitly reminds specialists to activate the Agentforce Agent in the target production org after deployment completes. Even if the agent was active in the sandbox, it lands inactive in production and won't respond to any conversation until manually activated there — which matches the symptom described (fails to respond to any test messages, even though the Apex action and API are both confirmed working). There's no "Production Ready" checkbox on agents (A) — that's a fictional setting. Option C is contradicted by the question itself, which states the API endpoint is reachable; an authentication problem also wouldn't cause total silence on every message, which is the classic signature of an inactive agent instead. [Verificado con búsqueda web: confirmado que la activación del agente no se preserva en el deploy y debe hacerse manualmente en producción tras el deploy (gearset.com/blog/how-to-deploy-agentforce, trailhead "Deploy an AI Agent with Agentforce").]

### [Agentforce Specialist V2] {Data 360 Fundamentals} 30
A publishing company builds an agent to answer royalty payment questions. The agent retrieves data from two Data 360 indexes: one connected to internal contract files and another connected to an external sales reporting system. During testing, the agent gives inconsistent answers about royalty rates. The specialist needs to identify whether each piece of information came from the internal contracts or the external sales system. What is the most direct way to trace the source?
- [ ] A. Examine the "Index Source" column in the Data 360 data space settings, which logs every retrieval event with source attribution.
- [x] B. Run the same query in the Retriever Playground and inspect the data_source_name field returned with each chunk to see which index it belongs to.
- [ ] C. Add a post-processing step in the prompt template that asks the LLM to append "[INTERNAL]" or "[EXTERNAL]" to every sentence based on its own judgment.
> The Retriever Playground (already covered in this bank) is built precisely for isolating and inspecting retriever behavior: running the same query there returns each chunk along with its source metadata, letting the specialist trace exactly which index/data source each piece of grounding content came from — without depending on anything the LLM says about itself. Data 360 data space settings don't provide a per-retrieval event log with source attribution (A) — that's not a real feature. Asking the LLM to self-attribute sources with tags like "[INTERNAL]"/"[EXTERNAL]" (C) is unreliable, since the model can misidentify or hallucinate the source, defeating the point of an objective diagnosis. [Nota de confianza: el mecanismo general (Retriever Playground muestra metadata de origen por chunk) es consistente con lo ya verificado en la pregunta #23 de este lote, pero no pude confirmar el nombre literal del campo "data_source_name" en documentación oficial — verificar el nombre exacto del campo en el org antes de memorizarlo.]

### [Agentforce Specialist V2] {Governance & Observability} 31
A telecom company's customer agent keeps sending "billing dispute" conversations to the "plan upgrade" subagent, even when users explicitly mention overcharges or incorrect fees. The specialist has added guard conditions but the problem continues. What is the most likely root cause?
- [ ] A. The global system instructions contain conflicting directives that prioritize plan upgrades over billing disputes.
- [ ] B. The "plan upgrade" subagent has a higher numerical priority setting than the billing dispute subagent.
- [x] C. The classification descriptions for the two subagents have significant semantic overlap, confusing the planner.
> Same mechanism confirmed repeatedly in this bank: the planner selects a subagent by matching user input against each subagent's Topic Name and Classification Description, so persistent misrouting — even after adding guard conditions, which only gate actions/subagents once selected, not the initial classification step — points to semantic overlap between the two classification descriptions themselves. Global system instructions (A) apply broadly across all subagents and don't create a selection conflict between two specific subagents. There is no numerical priority setting for subagents (B); routing is semantic matching, not a weighted ranking system — this is an invented distractor mechanism. [Mismo patrón ya verificado en las preguntas #1, #11 y #18 de este banco; no requirió verificación adicional.]

### [Agentforce Specialist V2] {Multi-Agent Orchestration} 32 — ⚠️ DISPUTADA, verificar en org real
An e-commerce agent has an "Apply Discount" action restricted by the guard `available when @user.verified = true`. During a single conversation turn, the LLM successfully sets `verified = true` using `@utils.setVariables`, but then fails to call the "Apply Discount" action in the same turn. Why does this happen?
- [ ] A. The action's availability condition re-evaluates instantly after each variable change, but the LLM's reasoning cycle cannot keep up within the same turn.
- [x] B. The guard condition is evaluated once at the start of the reasoning cycle; variable changes made during the turn do not trigger re-evaluation until the next turn. *(respuesta dada por la fuente del usuario — marcada [x] por continuidad de formato, pero ver nota de discrepancia abajo)*
- [ ] C. The LLM must explicitly request a "refresh availability" call before the action becomes visible, which the specialist forgot to include.
> ⚠️ CORRECCIÓN / DISPUTA — a diferencia del resto de este lote, esta respuesta NO pudo confirmarse; de hecho la evidencia oficial apunta en la dirección contraria. La guía oficial de Agent Script ("AvailableWhenFiltering" recipe, developer.salesforce.com/sample-apps/agent-script-recipes/action-configuration/available-when-filtering, verificada contra un org real con `sf agent preview`) muestra un caso documentado donde, en un SOLO turno del usuario ("Look up ticket X and assign it to Sarah"), el agente ejecuta `view_ticket` (que actualiza `ticket_status` vía su propio `set`), y ACTO SEGUIDO —dentro de esa misma respuesta— usa `assign_ticket`, cuya disponibilidad depende de esa variable recién actualizada. Esto indica que el ciclo de razonamiento SÍ itera y re-evalúa las condiciones `available when` múltiples veces dentro de un mismo turno de usuario, contradiciendo la premisa de la Opción B (que dice que la re-evaluación espera al siguiente turno). Matiz no resuelto: el ejemplo oficial usa un `set` declarativo ligado a la propia acción, no `@utils.setVariables` (la utilidad que el LLM invoca para extraer datos de la conversación, ya documentada en este banco); no encontré confirmación de que ambos mecanismos se comporten de forma idéntica en cuanto a timing. Ninguna de las 3 opciones dadas describe con precisión el comportamiento que sí pude confirmar (re-evaluación dentro del mismo turno), así que mantuve la marca [x] original de la fuente por no tener una opción mejor que marcar, pero esta pregunta necesita verificación directa en un org antes de confiar en ella para el examen. [Verificado con búsqueda web: contradicción encontrada contra developer.salesforce.com/sample-apps/agent-script-recipes/action-configuration/available-when-filtering — confianza alta en que la Opción B, tal como está redactada, es incorrecta; confianza baja en cuál de las 3 opciones sería la "correcta" real.]

### [Agentforce Specialist V2] {AI Agents} 33
A mortgage lender's agent must perform credit checks and income verification in a strict sequence to comply with regulations. The agent also needs to respond flexibly to borrower questions. Which statement correctly differentiates declarative and procedural instructions in Agent Script's hybrid reasoning model?
- [ ] A. Declarative instructions guarantee execution order using -> prefixes, while procedural instructions allow the LLM to reorder steps for natural conversation.
- [ ] B. Declarative instructions are ignored in production environments; only procedural instructions enforce business rules.
- [x] C. Declarative instructions give the LLM conversational flexibility, while procedural instructions (using ->, run, if) enforce a guaranteed execution sequence.
> This is the exact hybrid reasoning definition already established and worded this same way elsewhere in this bank: declarative (natural-language) instructions let the LLM interpret and respond conversationally, while procedural instructions — marked with the `->` prefix and built from deterministic constructs like `run`, `if`, `set`, `transition` — execute in a guaranteed, code-like sequence, which is exactly what's needed for compliance steps (credit check, then income verification) that can never be skipped or reordered. Option A reverses which side owns the `->` prefix — it's procedural, not declarative, that uses it. Option B is simply false: both instruction types are active simultaneously in production; hybrid reasoning is precisely about combining them in the same agent, not disabling one. [Terminología y mecanismo ya verificados en este banco (definición de hybrid reasoning, casos KYC/Golden Bank y airline refund agent); no requirió verificación adicional.]

### [Agentforce Specialist V2] {AI Agents} 34
A property management company's agent must check if a maintenance request is within warranty before dispatching a technician. The company wants to keep the conversation natural for tenants but ensure the warranty check always happens first. What should the specialist do?
- [x] A. Use procedural instructions in Agent Script to enforce the warranty check step before any technician dispatch action.
- [ ] B. Move the warranty check logic into a separate agent and route all maintenance requests through that agent first.
- [ ] C. Add a natural language instruction at the top of the subagent prompt saying "Always check warranty before dispatching."
> Same hybrid reasoning design principle already established repeatedly in this bank: a mandatory, order-sensitive business step (the warranty check) belongs in procedural (`->`) instructions, which execute deterministically and can't be skipped, while the rest of the conversation with the tenant stays flexible and natural-language driven. This keeps everything in one agent instead of fragmenting the experience. Splitting the warranty check into a separate agent (B) is unnecessary architectural overhead that risks breaking conversational continuity — the same problem procedural instructions solve within a single agent. A natural-language instruction telling the LLM to "always check warranty before dispatching" (C) is non-deterministic and can be skipped or reordered by the LLM, which is exactly the failure mode hybrid reasoning is designed to prevent. [Consistente con el principio de hybrid reasoning ya verificado varias veces en este banco; no requirió verificación adicional.]

### [Agentforce Specialist V2] {Governance & Observability} 35
A retail chain needs to create Data 360 reports to analyze how customers interact with their shopping assistant. Which data lake object represents a complete container that captures all turns and messages from the start to the end of a single user-agent conversation?
- [ ] A. AIAgentConversation
- [x] B. AIAgentSession
- [ ] C. AIAgentTurn
> Confirmed directly against Salesforce's official Session Tracing Data Model documentation: AIAgentSession is a real data lake/model object representing the session-level container (with related objects like AIAgentSessionParticipant tracking who's in it). The turn/message-level detail lives in separate related objects — AIAgentInteraction (a single exchange), AIAgentInteractionStep, and AIAgentInteractionMessage — not in an object called "AIAgentTurn" (C), which doesn't exist under that name; "AIAgentConversation" (A) also isn't a real object in this data model. [Verificado con búsqueda web contra la página oficial "Data Model for Agentforce Session Tracing" (help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ai.generative_ai_session_trace_data_model.htm) — confirmé los nombres exactos AIAgentSession, AIAgentSessionParticipant, AIAgentInteraction, AIAgentInteractionStep, AIAgentInteractionMessage.]

### [Agentforce Specialist V2] {Testing, Deployment & Maintenance} 36
A nonprofit organization uses only no-code tools. They have many small donors who give sporadically. They want to prepare their fundraising team for calls by: summarizing past donations, showing events the donor attended, and recapping email conversations. Which approach should the specialist recommend?
- [ ] A. Export all donor data to a CSV and manually create summaries in a document.
- [x] B. Use a prompt template grounded on CRM and Data 360 data with standard foundation models.
- [ ] C. Fine-tune a large language model on the donor data to generate custom summaries.
> Same pattern already established in this bank (the Universal Containers sales-ops call-prep scenario): a no-code prompt template grounded on CRM and Data Cloud/Data 360 data, using a standard foundation model, can synthesize past donations, event attendance, and email history into a call-prep summary without any custom development. Manually exporting to CSV and writing summaries by hand (A) isn't scalable and defeats the purpose of automating this for a busy fundraising team. Fine-tuning a model on donor data (C) requires ML/coding expertise that violates the stated no-code constraint and is unnecessary overkill for a grounded-summarization use case that standard models already handle well. ### [Agentforce Specialist V2] {AI Agents} 37
A logistics company built a custom Apex action that an employee agent calls to fetch real-time shipment tracking from an external carrier API. The Apex method uses UserInfo.getSessionId() to authenticate the callout. The callout works when tested in the UI but fails silently when the agent triggers it. What is the best practice fix?

- [x] B. Replace the session ID retrieval with a Named Credential configured for the external API.
- [ ] C. Store the session ID in a custom label and reference it in the Apex callout.
> Named Credentials are Salesforce's standard best practice for authenticating external callouts — they store and manage credentials securely and work reliably regardless of execution context, unlike `UserInfo.getSessionId()`, which depends on having a valid interactive UI session and can behave unreliably when Apex is invoked from a background/system context like an agent action. `with sharing` (A) controls record-level visibility for SOQL/DML, not external callout authentication — irrelevant to this failure. Custom labels (C) store static, org-wide strings; a session ID is per-user and dynamic, so it can't correctly live in a label. [Buenas prácticas estándar de Salesforce (Named Credentials para callouts externos) ya bien establecidas; no requirió verificación adicional más allá de confirmación general.]

### [Agentforce Specialist V2] {Governance & Observability} 39
A bank's service agent can access sensitive account transaction data only after the customer completes voice biometric verification. The specialist needs a deterministic control that prevents the LLM from bypassing verification to run the "Show Transactions" action. What should they configure?
- [x] A. Apply an availability filter (available when) on the "Show Transactions" action so it is hidden from the planner until a verification variable becomes true.
- [ ] B. Add a system instruction that says "Never show transactions without verification" and place it in every subagent.
- [ ] C. Store the transaction data in an encrypted field and only decrypt it after the LLM requests verification.
> Same deterministic-guard pattern already verified multiple times in this bank (Issue Refund/Account_Tier, Apply Discount/verified, KYC/hybrid reasoning): an `available when` filter on the action makes it completely invisible to the planner until the verification variable evaluates to true, so the LLM literally cannot select or call it — a programmatic guarantee, not a suggestion. A system instruction telling every subagent to "never show transactions without verification" (B) is non-deterministic and can be ignored or misapplied by the LLM. Encrypting the data (C) doesn't stop the action itself from being called — the LLM could still invoke it and the action could still attempt to return (encrypted or decrypted) data; encryption protects data at rest/in transit, not action-level access control. ### [Agentforce Specialist V2] {Testing, Deployment & Maintenance} 40

### [Agentforce Specialist V2] {Prompt Engineering} 41
MediCare Plus needs a prompt to extract prescription name and dosage from patient emails. Which practice will produce the most consistent and accurate extraction?
- [ ] A. Use a high creativity setting (temperature 0.9) to allow the model to infer missing dosage information.
- [x] B. Provide two example emails with the correct extracted fields and set the temperature close to zero.
- [ ] C. Ask the model to first list all medications it sees, then select the primary prescription.
> For structured field extraction, few-shot examples (showing the exact input-output pattern desired) combined with a near-zero temperature is the standard best practice: low temperature minimizes output randomness/hallucination, and the examples teach the model precisely what format and fields to extract, together producing the most consistent, repeatable results. A high temperature (A) does the opposite of what extraction needs — it increases variability and the risk of the model inventing ("inferring") dosage information that isn't actually in the email, which is dangerous in a medical context. Asking the model to first list all medications and then pick the primary one (C) adds unnecessary multi-step reasoning complexity, extra latency/token cost, and more surface area for errors, for a task that's fundamentally simple field extraction. [Principios básicos y bien establecidos de prompt engineering (few-shot + low temperature para extracción determinista); no requirió verificación adicional.]

### [Agentforce Specialist V2] {AI Agents} 42
GreenLeaf Energy has an agent that calculates solar panel warranty discounts based on installation date. The agent must quote the exact discount amount and reuse the same number when generating the final confirmation. How should they ensure deterministic storage and reuse?
- [x] A. Store the discount in a context variable via a flow action and have the agent reference that variable in all responses.
- [ ] B. Instruct the agent in its system prompt to "remember this discount amount for later.”
- [ ] C. Recalculate the discount each time by re-executing the same formula from the agent's memory.
> Storing the flow-calculated discount in a variable — the same deterministic variable-storage pattern already established in this bank (Agent Script's `mutable`/`set`/`@utils.setVariables` mechanics) — guarantees the exact number is persisted once and then simply referenced verbatim afterward, eliminating any risk of the LLM re-generating, rounding, or "misremembering" the figure across turns. Telling the agent via system prompt to "remember this discount for later" (B) is non-deterministic — LLMs don't have guaranteed persistent memory of specific numbers purely from an instruction, and the value could drift or be restated incorrectly. Recalculating the discount every time from "the agent's memory" (C) is also unreliable — it depends on the model re-deriving the same formula and inputs correctly each time, risking inconsistent values instead of just reusing the one authoritative number already computed. [Consistente con el mecanismo de variables deterministas de Agent Script ya verificado en este banco; no requirió verificación adicional.]

### [Agentforce Specialist V2] {Governance & Observability} 43

Prompt Defense (A) is a distinct Trust Layer safeguard against prompt injection attacks, not a data-grounding mechanism. Output Caching (C) isn't a real named Einstein Trust Layer component in this context — even if some caching exists for performance elsewhere, it wouldn't inject live/fresh data and could actually return stale results, the opposite of what's needed here. ### [Agentforce Specialist V2] {Governance & Observability} 45
HealthFirst Clinic has a Private organization-wide default on the Patient Record object. An agent running a flow to retrieve patient records returns nothing even though records exist and the flow is correct. Which fix follows the principle of least privilege?

- [ ] B. Change the OWD on Patient Record to Public Read Only so the agent can see all patient records.
- [ ] C. Set the flow to run in System Mode without sharing to bypass all security.
> Standard Salesforce security best practice: granting the agent's running user profile explicit object permissions plus targeted sharing rules gives it exactly the access it needs for its task while leaving the Private OWD intact for everyone else — the textbook least-privilege fix. Changing OWD to Public Read Only (B) exposes every patient record to every user in the org, a massive over-grant for a healthcare/PHI context. Running the flow in System Mode without sharing (C) bypasses all record-level security entirely for that flow, which technically "fixes" the symptom but grants far more access than necessary and violates least privilege just as much as option B. ### [Agentforce Specialist V2] {Prompt Engineering} 53

### [Agentforce Specialist V2] {AI Agents} 58
Academy of Arts wants students to be able to ask its enrollment agent to check available class slots and enroll themselves directly through conversation, with the enrollment logic reusing validation rules that already exist as a declarative automation in the org. - [ ] B. An Apex trigger on the Enrollment object, since triggers can be called directly by agent actions.
- [ ] C. A Visualforce page embedded in the agent's response.
> Mismo patrón ya establecido en este banco: los Auto-launched Flows son el tipo de acción estándar para exponer lógica declarativa (validaciones, actualizaciones de registros) como acciones de agente sin escribir código, y permiten reutilizar automatización ya construida en la org. Los Apex triggers (B) no son invocables directamente como acciones de agente — se invocan por eventos DML, no por el planner del agente — y una Visualforce page (C) es tecnología de UI heredada, no un mecanismo de acción de agente. [Consistente con el uso extendido de Flows como acciones de agente ya verificado en este banco; no requirió verificación adicional.]

### [Agentforce Specialist V2] {Agent Script} 59
GreenStay Hotels' agent needs to send a booking confirmation email immediately after successfully processing a reservation, as part of the same deterministic sequence, without waiting for the LLM to decide whether to do it. Which Agent Script keyword lets the specialist chain that action to run right after the reservation action completes?
- [x] A. `run`
- [ ] B. `mutable`
- [ ] C. `available when`
> Consistente con la sintaxis de Agent Script ya confirmada en este banco (páginas oficiales de recetas AfterReasoning y AvailableWhenFiltering fetchadas anteriormente en esta sesión): `run @actions.x` se usa para encadenar la ejecución inmediata y determinista de una acción dentro de un bloque procedural, sin dejarlo a discreción del LLM. `mutable` (B) declara una variable como modificable en tiempo de ejecución — no encadena acciones — y `available when` (C) es la guarda que controla si una acción es visible/seleccionable, no un mecanismo de encadenamiento inmediato. [Consistente con sintaxis de Agent Script ya verificada en este banco; no requirió verificación adicional.]

### [Agentforce Specialist V2] {Governance & Observability} 60
Coastline Credit Union needs a weekly dashboard for its leadership team showing agent deflection and escalation trends over time, without building custom reports from scratch. Which native Agentforce Observability capability should the specialist point them to?
- [x] A. Agent Analytics, which provides prebuilt, Tableau-powered dashboards covering deflection, abandonment, escalations, and volume trends.
- [ ] B. The raw Session Tracing Data Model objects, queried manually via SOQL each week.
- [ ] C. Testing Center pass/fail results, exported to a spreadsheet weekly.

Consultar manualmente los objetos del Session Tracing Data Model vía SOQL (B) es la opción "hazlo tú mismo" para casos avanzados/custom, no la vía nativa pensada para un dashboard de liderazgo listo para usar. Testing Center (C) mide resultados de pruebas antes de producción, no tendencias de uso en producción. [Verificado con búsqueda web: Agent Analytics confirmado como real, Tableau-powered, con las métricas de deflection/abandonment/escalations mencionadas.]

### [Agentforce Specialist V2] {AI Agents} 61
NovaTech Logistics wants to empower its support representatives to check real-time shipment tracking details using plain conversational language. A pre-built autolaunched flow already exists to pull data from SAP, the company's system of record for logistics operations. How should an Agentforce Specialist best extend this capability using conversational AI?

"Sales Coach" (A) es una plantilla orientada a coaching de ventas, no a consultas de sistemas externos. No existe una acción estándar "Logistics Query" en Agentforce Builder (B) — las integraciones con sistemas externos como SAP requieren custom actions respaldadas por flow o Apex. ### [Agentforce Specialist V2] {AI Agents} 62
An Agentforce Specialist at SunVista Hotels is tasked with building an AI agent to handle guest dissatisfaction cases automatically. The agent should be capable of offering room upgrades, dining credits, and complimentary amenities. When a guest experiences a severe service failure — such as an overbooking — the agent must escalate the case to a live representative. Per Salesforce best practices, which agent type should the specialist deploy?

- [x] C. Service Agent with a Flex prompt template.

Einstein Copilot con plantilla de ventas (A) está orientado a coaching de vendedores, no a quejas de huéspedes. Un Employee Agent (B) está pensado para casos de uso internos (IT helpdesk, RRHH), no interacciones con huéspedes externos. ### [Agentforce Specialist V2] {Agent Script} 63
MediCore Clinics is refining its patient intake agent to meet strict regulatory requirements. The compliance officer has mandated that agents must confirm a patient's identity before any downstream action — such as booking a lab test — can be triggered. The verification step must be enforced deterministically, blocking all subsequent actions until it is satisfied. What approach should the Agentforce Specialist recommend using standard configuration methods?
- [ ] A. Write a custom Lightning Web Component that monitors agent session state and hides scheduling buttons until verification is confirmed.
- [ ] B. Apply dynamic template expressions inside the scheduling action description to display a verification warning when the patient is unverified.
- [x] C. Update a mutable session variable for verification status using `@utils.setVariables`, then control the lab booking action visibility with an `available when` condition.
> Mismo patrón determinista de Agent Script ya verificado varias veces en este banco: escribir el estado de verificación en una variable de sesión mutable vía `@utils.setVariables` y condicionar la disponibilidad de la acción posterior con `available when` es el mecanismo declarativo estándar — la acción queda físicamente invisible para el motor de razonamiento hasta que la variable sea verdadera. Un LWC (A) opera en la capa de UI, no en el motor de razonamiento del agente, y no bloquea la acción de forma determinista. Las expresiones de plantilla en la descripción de la acción (B) solo afectan el texto mostrado, no si la acción puede invocarse. [Consistente con el patrón determinista de session variable + available when ya verificado varias veces en este banco; no requirió verificación adicional.]

### [Agentforce Specialist V2] {Custom Actions} 64
BrightPath Education is building a custom agent and has developed an Apex action that accepts a collection of course names as an input parameter (a list of strings). - [ ] C. `apex__StringList`
